chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, who said: Some of our companions narrated to us, as reported by Sa'd bin Turaif, from Asbagh bin Nubata, from Al-Harith al-A'war, who said: The Commander of the Believers said to his son Hasan, peace be upon them both, regarding some of what he asked him about: O my son, what is lenience? He said: Spending during distress and ease.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of lenience (samah) in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (AS) defines *samah* not merely as charity, but as a steadfast ethical disposition of giving freely in both scarcity and abundance, highlighting the consistency of the virtuous. This definition, transmitted through the chain of al-Asbagh ibn Nabatah, underscores the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence) in character, where generosity becomes a constant trait rather than a situational reaction. It serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain spiritual equilibrium and social responsibility regardless of economic fluctuations.
